newsitem.title: INDIA: India buys 50,000 t U.S. sunflowerseed oil - trader.
newsitem.headline: India buys 50,000 t U.S. sunflowerseed oil - trader.

text.p: India has contracted to import about 50,000 tonnes of sunflowerseed oil from the United States for shipment in December and January, Navinbhai Shah, president of the Bombay Oilseeds and Oil Exchange Ltd, said on Tuesday.

"India has contracted to import around 50,000 tonnes of sunflowerseed oil from the U.S. for December and January (shipment)," Shah told Reuters by telephone from his office in Bombay. No price details were immediately available.
On Monday, U.S. exporters said India recently bought 18,000 tonnes of U.S. sunflowerseed oil for December shipment from the Gulf of Mexico.
Chicago sources said it was believed the oil was bought for 0.10 U.S. cent per lb under CBOT December soybean oil futures.
"This year, the fall in the country's domestic production (of oilseeds) coupled with the freezing of the palm olein oil has pushed up the demand for sunflowerseed oil," Shah said.
"Therefore, the next acceptable edible oil in India is sunflowerseed oil," he said.
